transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-11-21 16:30 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Liu (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood SE), Ava Thompson (NorthStar CTO), Miguel Rivera (NorthStar ML Eng), Priya Kapoor (NorthStar VP Product)

Auto-summary: quick discovery on model choice - context length, multilingual, tool-calling, and deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private).

[00:00] Jamie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll kick off. I'm Jamie from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Carlos, our systems SE, who will do the deep dives.
[00:12] Ava: Hi - thanks, Jamie. Ava here. Quick context: we're NorthStar, we run a client-facing analytics platform across EU/US, lots of enterprise customers. We're evaluating LLM infra for insights automation and a conversational assistant that uses customer docs.
[00:27] Miguel: Hey all, Miguel. Main constraints: need 64k-ish context for large documents, bilingual to multilingual - EN/ES/FR ideally plus some low-resource languages, and function/tool calling to run retrieval + structured API outputs.
[00:36] Carlos: Got it. When you say 64k, is that peak or per-session persistent?
[00:39] Miguel: Peak per session, yeah, for cases where we stitch many docs; average session is more like 8-12k.
[00:46] Priya: Timeline wise we want to pilot in Q1 - pilot scope ~3 weeks, 1-2 internal apps and then expand. Security is a hard requirement: SOC2, EU data residency, SSO/SAML, KMS integration.
[00:58] Jamie: Great. On deployment mode - quick map: Hosted is fastest to onboard and good for cost, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity for predictable latency and throughput, and Private gives you VPC/on-prem for strict data residency and control. There are tradeoffs around unit cost and setup time.
[01:15] Ava: We're leaning away from pure hosted because of data residency and compliance; Dedicated or Private look more realistic, but cost is a concern.
[01:22] Carlos: Totally reasonable. For Dedicated you can get the reserved capacity and private networking options; Private (VPC or on-prem) means you control the infra and keys. We also have a Private control plane option that eases management while keeping data inside your VPC.
[01:34] Miguel: On model selection - we currently prototype with an open LLM, like Llama variants, and tried a 70B that we quantized. We saw memory issues at 64k. Curious what Redwood's suggestions are for model family, quantization, and inference perf.
[01:49] Carlos: A few practical notes: architecture matters - 70B models can hit memory for 64k unless you're using optimized kernels + KV cache management and 4-bit quantization. We recommend checking both sequence-length-optimized checkpoints and model variants with longer-context configs. Redwood runtime picks kernels based on seq len and hardware.
[02:08] Priya: Do you have recommended models for multilingual support? Also, how is function-calling handled - native function calls or do we need an orchestration layer?
[02:19] Jamie: For multilingual, we usually point customers to models trained multilingual (Mosaic, Mistral forks, some Llama-derivatives) - depends on the languages. We can share a model catalog with performance profiles. For function-calling, Redwood supports structured outputs and tool-calling; SE can show how we hook to RAG and external APIs.
[02:36] Miguel: Any gotchas with hallucinations when using retrieval plus tool calls? We need high precision on API outputs - can't have stray hallucinated fields in downstream invoices.
[02:47] Carlos: Yep - that's an implementation thing: use strong retrieval, prompt engineering, and output schemas. We also offer eval/quality monitoring so you can surface regressions tied to prompt sets.
[02:59] Ava: Perf targets - we want p95 < 400ms for short queries and p95 < 2s for long in the Dedicated tier. Are those realistic?
[03:09] Carlos: For short queries with smaller models or distilled variants that's achievable. For 64k context, p95 will be higher; you can design a hybrid: use long-context model only when needed and a cheaper fast model for short queries. Smart routing/fallback can keep SLA while managing cost.
[03:29] Priya: What's the cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated? Ballpark for our expected traffic?
[03:33] Jamie: Ballpark: Hosted is pay-as-you-go, unit cost higher but no commit. Dedicated is lower unit cost for a reserved commit; exact depends on capacity size and GPU generation. We'll send a tailored pricing grid.
[03:46] Miguel: About quantization - we tried 4-bit but saw weird tokenization artifacts on longer sequences. Does Redwood do model distillation or suggest specific quantization toolchains?
[03:57] Carlos: We don't do model training/distillation in-platform, but our Optimize toolkit recommends quantization profiles and kernel paths. For very long contexts we recommend sequence-length-aware checkpoints and careful kv cache tuning; SE-led perf tests help validate.
[04:13] Ava: Compliance questions: SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs retention windows - can you support EU-only residency and HSM-backed keys?
[04:23] Jamie: Yes - we support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and audit logs. For EU residency and HSM/KMS, Private or Dedicated with private networking + customer-managed KMS is the recommended path. We'll attach the SOC2/ISO and KMS integration docs.
[04:37] Miguel: For benchmarking, what do you need from us? Sample prompts or datasets?
[04:41] Carlos: Ideally: a representative set of prompts, exemplar docs for RAG, and traffic profile (tokens/session, sessions/day). We'll run latency, throughput, and cost-estimate tests for both Dedicated and Hosted.
[04:53] Priya: We also want to test multilingual fidelity - we'll provide EN/ES/FR prompts and some low-resource examples.
[04:59] Jamie: Perfect. We'll scope a 3-week pilot: SE perf tests in week 1, integration + RAG in week 2, user acceptance tests in week 3. Pilot success criteria: p95 latency targets for core flows, <2% hallucination rate on structured outputs, and acceptable unit cost.
[05:20] Ava: Sounds good. Any legal procurement lead time we should budget?
[05:24] Jamie: Enterprise procurement varies - for Dedicated/Private expect 4-8 weeks to finalize contracts; pilot can start faster under a limited pilot agreement.
[05:32] Miguel: Quick tech nit: you mentioned KV cache management earlier - sometimes transcribed as K V cash - can you explain briefly?
[05:39] Carlos: (laughs) Yeah, KV cache is the key-value cache used to store past attention states to avoid recomputation. Proper caching and continuous batching reduce cost and latency for long contexts. We'll demo it in the technical deep dive.
[05:54] Priya: Competitor angle - some stakeholders prefer Anthropic-style safety/guardrails; others like OpenAI for model quality. How does Redwood work with those?
[06:04] Jamie: We integrate multiple open and third-party models through our catalog and can route requests by policy. If you want specific guardrails, we can layer evals and quality monitors and combine model routing with reranking.
[06:18] Ava: Any constraints for on-prem? We're considering a private appliance for a subset of regulated customers.
[06:24] Carlos: On-prem adds ops overhead but gives maximal control. Redwood's Private deployment can be on your infra with a private control plane; we support KMS, audit logs, and offline upgrades for air-gapped deployments. We'll include architecture notes.
[06:40] Miguel: For the perf tests, can you do a run with 64k context on an MLC-like optimized kernel and also a 32k variant; we want p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens estimates.
[06:52] Carlos: Yep, we'll run both and include quantized and fp16 baselines.
[06:57] Jamie: Ok, to recap next steps - Jamie will send security docs and pricing; Carlos will schedule the 1h perf deep dive and run the benchmarks; Miguel will provide datasets and prompts. We'll aim to have the pilot SOW and pricing by Monday.
[07:11] Ava: Thanks, that works. We'll look out for the docs.
[07:15] Miguel: Quick question - is function-calling schema validation native or do we need middleware?
[07:20] Carlos: We support structured outputs and can enforce schemas at the runtime level; typically you also validate on the consumer side as a belt-and-suspenders approach.
[07:29] Priya: Alright, thanks everyone.
[07:31] Jamie: Thanks all. I'll follow up with the doc pack and calendar invites for the deep dive.
[07:35] Ava: Bye.

End of transcript.

References/Artifacts shared: link: /redwood/decks/model-catalog.pdf (sent after call), link: /redwood/docs/security-soc2.zip (to be sent), perf-benchmark-template.xlsx (placeholder link).
